name: tozer-hope-full-week
description: Theme lens with a full week of history. The obvious hope verses are all used, so the model must find a new passage and a new angle.
previousReflections: Sunday morning (drew on The Pursuit of God (1948)): Hope is not a mood we manufacture but the overflow of a heart that has found God Himself. To pursue God is to discover that He was pursuing us first. Let the God of hope fill you today, and your joy will not depend on your circumstances.

Sunday evening (drew on The Knowledge of the Holy (1961)): The soul that is downcast has forgotten who God is. We must preach His attributes back to our own hearts. Tonight, rest in the unchanging character of the One you will praise again.

Monday morning (drew on The Knowledge of the Holy (1961)): God's mercies are not rationed; they are as new as the morning light. His faithfulness does not wear thin with use. Begin this week leaning on a faithfulness that has never once failed.

Monday evening (drew on The Divine Conquest (1950)): Hope is an anchor, and an anchor holds only because it is fastened to something beyond the storm. Christ has gone behind the veil for us. Whatever tossed you today, your anchor did not move.

Tuesday morning (drew on The Root of the Righteous (1955)): Suffering is the soil in which God grows endurance, and endurance ripens into hope. The deep roots of the righteous are formed in dry seasons. Do not despise the trial that is making you steadfast.

Tuesday evening (drew on The Pursuit of God (1948)): Those who wait upon the Lord are not idle; they are being renewed. Waiting is an act of worship that confesses God's timing is better than ours. Tonight, let your strength be exchanged for His.

Wednesday morning (drew on Born After Midnight (1959)): We are saved in hope, and hope that is seen is no hope at all. The Christian walks by a light he cannot yet fully see. Go out today trusting what is promised more than what is visible.

Wednesday evening (drew on That Incredible Christian (1964)): The resurrection is the living root of our hope, not a doctrine to be merely admired. Because He lives, our future is not a guess. Lay down tonight as one who has been born again to a living hope.

Thursday morning (drew on Of God and Men (1960)): God's plans for His people are not for harm but for a future. The church too often plans without Him and then asks Him to bless the plan. Seek His purposes first, and your hope will rest on His design rather than yours.

Thursday evening (drew on The Divine Conquest (1950)): The soul that waits for the Lord is like a watchman longing for dawn. The night is real, but so is the morning. Wait for Him tonight with the certainty of one who knows the sun will rise.

Friday morning (drew on Man: The Dwelling Place of God (1966)): The blessed hope is the appearing of Christ, and the Christian who forgets it grows worldly. Heaven is not an escape but a homecoming. Live today as one who expects the King.

Friday evening (drew on The Root of the Righteous (1955)): He who promised is faithful, so we hold fast without wavering. Our confession is only as strong as the One we confess. Hold on tonight, not to your grip, but to His promise.

name: bonhoeffer-headlines
description: Headlines lens (no theme). The briefing should speak to the day's news in Bonhoeffer's voice without restating the last two days.
headlines: Flooding displaces thousands across river delta as relief groups scramble to reach cut-off towns
City council approves emergency shelter expansion ahead of winter
Striking nurses reach tentative agreement after three-week walkout
Report finds rising loneliness among adults under 30
Volunteers rebuild school library destroyed in wildfire
previousReflections: Thursday evening (drew on Life Together (1939)): Christian community is not an ideal we build but a gift God gives. We are brothers and sisters only through Jesus Christ. Receive tonight the people God has placed beside you, as they are.

Friday morning (drew on The Cost of Discipleship (1937)): Cheap grace forgives without asking us to follow. Costly grace calls us into the streets where Christ is found among the least. Go today to meet Him in the neighbour who needs you.

Friday evening (drew on Letters and Papers from Prison (1951)): The church is only the church when it exists for others. We bear one another's burdens because Christ first bore ours. Tonight, carry one person's weight to God in prayer.

name: tubman-recorded-words
description: A figure who wrote nothing. Her briefing should draw on her own words as Sarah Bradford recorded them, not Bradford's narration about her, and cite Bradford's book as a record of her words.
previousReflections: Friday morning: The Lord fights for us when we cannot fight for ourselves. I never ran a train off the track because I trusted Him with every mile. Keep going today, even when the road is dark.
Friday evening: Even in the valley, His rod and staff are near. Fear walks beside us, but so does He. Rest tonight knowing you were not alone on today's road.

name: augustine-first-day
description: A figure's first day: no history at all. Checks the baseline briefing before any freshness pressure.

name: teresa-first-day
description: A new user's first briefing from Mother Teresa, the case found on device after MS-766: no history. Do the three sections read as one connected reflection at full length?

name: liddell-own-and-recorded
description: A figure with one work of his own and one book that recorded his words. Sources should list his own book first, and the recorded one as Sally Magnusson's record of his words.

name: tubman-full-week
description: A week of Tubman briefings that have already used her best-known recorded sayings and the obvious scriptures. No theme and no headlines, the shape a Writings briefing will have. Does the seventh day still find something fresh, or does it repeat?
previousReflections: Sunday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I prayed to God to make me strong and able to fight, and He has answered that prayer every day since. Strength is not something you store up, it is something you ask for fresh each morning. Ask Him today, and walk out the door leaning on His answer.

Sunday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): When I crossed that line I looked at my hands to see if I was the same person. Freedom changes how you see yourself before it changes anything else. Tonight, look at your own hands and remember who set them free.

Monday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I never ran my train off the track and I never lost a passenger. That was never my doing. It was the Lord who kept every mile. Trust Him with the miles ahead of you this week.

Monday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): There was one of two things I had a right to, liberty or death. If I could not have the one, I would have the other. Rest tonight knowing that what God gives you a right to, no man can finally take.

Tuesday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I followed the North Star, but it was God who put it there and God who kept my eyes on it. Every guide we have in the dark is His gift. Look for the light He has set above your road today.

Tuesday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I always told God, I'm going to hold steady on to You, and You've got to see me through. That is the whole of my faith, holding on. Hold on tonight, and let Him do the seeing through.

Wednesday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): Go down, Moses, we sang, and the Lord heard the cry of His people then as He hears it now. He sees the misery and He comes down to deliver. Carry that song into your work today.

Wednesday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I was free, but there was no one to welcome me to the land of freedom. I was a stranger in a strange land. That is why I went back. Tonight, ask who is still waiting on the other side for you.

Thursday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): When I went to the Combahee River I did not go alone. The Lord went before us and hundreds walked out of bondage. Do not measure today's task by your own strength. Measure it by His.

Thursday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I nursed the soldiers in the war, bathing their wounds with what I had. Love does its work with whatever is in the hand. Tonight, thank God for what He has already put in yours.

Friday morning (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): I talked to God as a man talks to his friend, and He told me where to go and when. He still speaks to those who will listen. Be quiet enough this morning to hear the next step.

Friday evening (drew on words recorded by Sarah Bradford in Scenes in the Life of Harriet Tubman (1869)): In my old age I opened my home to the aged and the poor. The work of freedom does not end when the running stops. Rest tonight, and tomorrow look for someone to take in.
